cuts.raw_narration: A menacing female voice declares from the dark that she has a duty to fulfill — she must give birth to the king. An ominous cold-open hook.
The hunters examine a recovered claw the size of a human finger. Computer analysis matched it 99 percent to a chimera ant queen, hinting at a giant, possibly mutated species.
The researchers explain phago-genesis: when the chimera ant queen eats other creatures, she absorbs their traits and passes a mix of those genes down to her offspring.

The queen hunts the strongest organisms and can devour her favorite prey to extinction, eating many times her body weight in a day. Judging by the claw she is at least two meters long — big enough to eat a human in seconds.

A quiet family moment: the mother praises nine-year-old Kurt as reliable and asks him to keep looking after his little sister Reina. Kurt promises he will keep both of them safe no matter what happens.
The queen savors new prey, moaning that it is delicious and the most nutritious fodder yet, and commands that she must consume more of this species — clearly humans.

The queen orders her newborn talking squadron leader to capture more of the highly nutritious humans. The narrator lands the reveal: a chimera ant has been born with human genes, and the researcher's worst fears have finally come to pass.
